title: What's New: AL-Go for GitHub on Security (2025 release wave 1)

features.name: Deprecations Website
features.description: Website explaining features that will be deprecated in the future with changes that will stop working after October 1st and build warnings for deprecated features.
caveats: Features listed without version numbers in release notes have not been released yet

features.name: Azure Trusted Signing Integration
features.description: Integration with Azure Trusted Signing service that eliminates manual certificate rotation and secret storage for code signing. Requires creating an Azure account, identity validation, certificate profile, managed identity, federated credentials, and trusted signing settings in GitHub repository.
caveats: Requires identity validation which is described as the hardest step

features.name: GitHub App Authentication
features.description: Authentication method using GitHub app ID and private key to create short-lived access tokens instead of personal access tokens. Tokens are scoped to specific permissions and organizations, with no user impersonation. Each access token only has permissions needed for its specific operation.
caveats: Does not work with GitHub packages feature; personal access token with packages reader permission required as workaround

features.name: Embed Secrets in Install Apps
features.description: Feature that allows storing install app URLs and SAS tokens in GitHub secrets instead of plain text in source code. Enables installing apps without exposing sensitive URLs or tokens in logs or repository.

features.name: Multiple Branches Workflow Support
features.description: Capability added in version 6.4 to update AL-Go system files on multiple branches at a time. New workflow schedule setting allows defining cron schedule and list of branches to include when running update workflow.
caveats: GitHub limitation does not allow scheduling for multiple branches that are not the default branch
